user.title: Which LibrePower instance?
user.description: Pick the LibrePower core installation this Powerwall belongs to.

powerwall.title: Connect your Powerwall
powerwall.description:
This adapter talks to the Gateway directly over your local network. You only need the Gateway password printed on the Powerwall itself — no Tesla account required for telemetry.

Your Home Assistant host must be able to reach the Gateway. If 192.168.91.1 doesn't respond, you may need a static route or to join the Gateway's WiFi network.

Battery capacity and charge/discharge limits are entered here because pypowerwall has no way to read them from the device automatically — use your Powerwall's nameplate rating (13500 Wh per unit is standard).

Charge/discharge efficiency default to 0.90 if left as-is - a reasonable placeholder, not a measured value. Override only if you have a better manufacturer figure for your specific hardware.

reauth_confirm.title: Powerwall password changed
reauth_confirm.description: The Gateway is no longer accepting the stored password. Re-enter the password printed on the Powerwall.

connection_method.title: How should this connect to your Powerwall?
connection_method.description: Most setups use the gateway password printed on the Powerwall. If you'd rather not open the unit to read it, you can pair with your Tesla account instead - no password needed, ever, for reads or writes. Pairing needs a PW3 on wired LAN, a Tesla account, and a one-time physical breaker toggle to confirm.

powerwall_v1r.title: Connect your Powerwall
powerwall_v1r.description:
Pairing is done - this just needs the Gateway's address on your regular network (its wired LAN IP, not the 192.168.91.1 WiFi AP address - pure v1r connects directly, no AP join needed) and your Powerwall's hardware specs.

Battery capacity and charge/discharge limits are entered here because pypowerwall has no way to read them from the device automatically — use your Powerwall's nameplate rating (13500 Wh per unit is standard).

Charge/discharge efficiency default to 0.90 if left as-is - a reasonable placeholder, not a measured value. Override only if you have a better manufacturer figure for your specific hardware.

pair_login.title: Log in to Tesla

pair_site.title: Which Powerwall?
pair_site.description: Multiple energy sites were found on this Tesla account - pick the one this adapter connects to.

pair_toggle.title: Confirm on the Gateway
pair_toggle.description: Tesla didn't auto-verify the key from the cloud step alone. Toggle ONE Powerwall breaker (the DC isolator) OFF, wait a couple of seconds, then back ON - this is Tesla's own physical-presence check, not something this integration can do for you. Then submit this form to check again; it's fine to submit more than once if it's still pending.

pair_success.title: Pairing complete

error.invalid_gateway_password: The Gateway rejected that password. Check the sticker on the Powerwall — it's the full string, not just the last few characters.
error.gateway_unreachable: Couldn't reach the Gateway at that address. Check that Home Assistant has a network route to it.
error.unknown: Unexpected error — check the Home Assistant logs.
error.pairing_auth_error: Tesla rejected that login - the pasted URL may be from an old attempt, or the code may have expired. Try opening the login URL again.
error.pairing_no_site: No Powerwall/energy site was found on that Tesla account - make sure you logged in with the account the Powerwall is actually set up under.
error.pairing_still_pending: Still not verified. Make sure you toggled the breaker off and back on, then submit again - it can take a few seconds to register.
error.pairing_error: Something went wrong talking to Tesla - check the Home Assistant logs for detail.

abort.already_configured: This Powerwall is already registered with that LibrePower instance.
abort.core_not_configured: No LibrePower instance found. Install and set up the LibrePower core integration first, then add this one.

init.title: Pair for battery control
init.description:
{status}

The gateway password you already entered is enough for read-only telemetry. Writing to the battery (charge, discharge, curtailment, islanding) needs an RSA key registered with Tesla and physically confirmed on the Gateway - this does not replace the gateway password, it adds to it. This uses your own Tesla account login directly (the same one the Tesla app uses) - no developer account, no third-party service.
